This is a very tentative recommendation, as while I enjoyed it, there are a couple things that are almost required to do so. First of all, cursor hints are basically mandatory, so turn those on immediately. Also, and I really don't care if this seems like a cop-out, MAXIMIZE YOUR BRIGHTNESS SETTINGS (turning up gamma helps too). The environments are so dang dark that it becomes really hard to enjoy otherwise in many places.

Once I could actually see everything I was mostly fine. There are a few bonkers puzzles that are annoying to solve (some of the password puzzles are a bit ridiculous). Though I didn't have too much trouble with any of the sliding puzzles (yes, including that stupid concentric rings one, which took me about ten minutes), I can absolutely see why many hated those, so YMMV (the critical path ones are skippable though, which is nice).

Enjoyable. Solid game.
Most puzzles were logical, and not too obscure, and had a good sense of progression.

My biggest gripe, though not a large one is there is a fair bit of "hidden object" type searching which isn't my favorite. Most of the time it's fine, but sometimes (and given your perspective allows for 360 degree panning), it can be quite difficult to find all items from a POV. As an example, having the sliver of a corner of a book being your only hotspot in a sea of books... even with cursor hints on, many times these require a guide to locate.

Others have stated this better than I could already. If you don't mind a lot of pixel hunting and trying to see obscured buttons/trinkets/pull chains in dark, dingy environments, you might have fun with this game. 

Most of the game is just that, clicking on a lot of the background spots or hovering your mouse to find objects of interesting. 

Some of the puzzles are... out there. And some don't even follow their own logic. As an example, there is a point where you need to use a different base for a number problem...but the game doesn't use the numbering system correctly. Think of it like binary being 1 and 2 instead of 0 and 1.

Most of the puzzles involve trying to find the hidden key/fidget and putting them somewhere. Very one dimensional puzzles. And quite a few are "hidden" in very non-intuitive ways. 

Probably the worst puzzles aren't "hard" puzzles, just tedious. There is a series of fix the picture puzzles that you can either choose to skip or waste a good 10-40 minutes on trying to rotate the pieces correctly. Due to how it is implementing, it's more frustrating than challenging. 

Overall, I can't really recommend the game due to how tedious it is. It sucks up a lot of time with only a few moments of "Aha, I solved a puzzle!" mini-celebrations. It's a game that doesn't respect a player's time and feels very much from an older generation of PC games that padded playing time with little, repetitive tasks. 

I would recommend The Room series for a better set of games. I am tempted to say The House of Da Vinci as well but that one is middling at best.

[h1]先说结论：强烈推荐，绝对是解谜游戏爱好者不能错过的作品[/h1]
但是，仅限解谜游戏爱好者。如果你只是因为玩过The Room、锈湖这类游戏就觉得自己是“解谜游戏爱好者”的话，我建议谨慎入手，先领个免费的Demo试试看。
[h2] 先说优点：[/h2] 
1.游戏是3D指向点击类，地图很大，内容丰富（我全收集全成就通关花了接近12小时）。
2.地图分了很多区，每个区域都不大，单个区域谜题也不多，这个区域拿到的道具不能带到别的区域（会暂时隐藏，回到这个区域会再重新出现），有效降低解谜成本（道具总量还是很多的）。
3.谜题很精巧，也很讲道理，大部分谜题不需要“灵光一闪”或者和作者对电波；故事也比较有意思。
4.官方没有汉化，但是网上能搜到汉化补丁。
[h2]但是，缺点也很明显：[/h2]
1.除了开头室外，进到城堡以后场景非常非常非常黑（真的建议亮度拉满，就别管啥游戏氛围了）。
2.游戏从头到尾都没有引导，甚至文字都不多，不少道具完全没有提示，需要你先看到谜题本身才能和道具对上号。
3.如前文所述，地图很大，分了很多区域。虽然每个区域都不大，但是架不住多啊，而且某些谜题需要在各个区域之间穿梭，很容易迷路。
4.全成就和全收集要素藏的非常非常非常深……追求全成就全收集的玩家得痛苦一段时间了……
但总体，瑕不掩瑜，推荐！

- When you are done with a puzzle or finding things in an area of a room you can't click on it anymore, saving you time from looking in places that won't help you anymore.
- You can't click on objects that are not clues or puzzles
- Most puzzles can be solved with clues in the nearby area
- The atmosphere and graphics are nice

- There are a ton of collectibles to find (coins, etc.)

Cons (for me):
- There are a ton of collectibles to find (coins, etc.)
- Many areas are quite dark making it hard to see things, like the obscure chain up in the dark corner I need to pull to open a gate even though I swear I searched that area already like three times and my eyes hurt from the eye strain

I feel like if I had the same puzzles but in a smaller space with a wee bit more light, it would have been more enjoyable for me.

I'm a lifelong adventure player.  I started with Colossal Cave on an IBM 370 in 1978, and have always favored adventure games.  I am dogged and persistent, but I'm uninstalling Eyes of Ara without finishing it.

I ended up locked in the water channel room with the concentric rings puzzle.  After fiddling with it for over an hour (maybe several hours - I lost track), I looked up hints, but the hints said that I was just going to have to fiddle with it until I got it (a mathematician gave a helpful "bump", but even he said that you just have to keep fiddling with it).

It used to be that lazy adventure designers would put a "slider" puzzle or a maze in the game.  Nowadays, the lazy puzzle design is the "interlocked pieces" puzzle.  The concentric rings puzzle could only be logically solved by an advanced mathematician.  A savant could crack it intuitively, but if your not an advanced mathematician or a savant, you're stuck with fiddling it for hours.  Not fun!

Eyes of Ara has pretty good ambiance, decent graphics (I ended up turning brightness and gamma all the way up), and good/very good game controls and dynamics.  The storyline is "Meh" - okay, but not compelling.  But being locked in a room with a puzzle that requires hours of grinding?  It's just not worth the effort.

Edit:  Steam says that my play time was 3.6 hours, but the game itself says over 17 hours.

Pretty sad about this one. It starts off promising, but the vast, vast, VAST majority of challenge in this game comes from pixel hunting essential puzzle pieces in dark/muddy looking environments. Once you actually have all the pieces, the solution is (most of the time) obvious. You'll spend 70-80% of your playtime wracking your brain trying to figure something out, only to realize that you just don't have a vital part of the solution, and it really galls after a while.

Just a tip for any passing puzzle game devs, because it seems at least one of them needs reminding: a puzzle is meant to be a logic challenge. It is a scenario set up specifically to test your ability to intuit a path toward an end goal. That end goal MUST be made clear to the player, because if they don't understand what they're meant to be achieving, then they won't be able to engage with the challenge properly. A proper, well designed puzzle will provide the player with both a clear picture of what the end goal is, and provide them ALL the pieces needed to get there.

The challenge must come from putting the pieces together in the correct way. The challenge must absolutely NOT come from running through a castle, clicking on every single pixel trying to find the pieces that the game has hidden from you. Sudoku works as a puzzle because you start by knowing the pieces (the digits 1-9), and the solution (a filled grid with no repeats in rows, columns, or boxes). The challenge of sudoku lies in figuring out the configuration of the pieces, as it should with any well-designed puzzle.

This game just fails to structure it's 'puzzles' properly. It presents you with a round peg and a round hole, but it hides the peg behind a loose brick in a hallway wall hidden behind a wardrobe inside of a caged-off room. Putting the pieces together is a no-brainer, it's finding the damned things is what will take mental toll on you.

A fun point and click, find-the-pixel puzzle game. Not quite on par with The Room series, but interesting and challenging puzzles and decent game length.

Finding objects can be very hard because you have to search from fixed viewpoints unlike games with free movement where you can walk up and get closer.  The environments are also very cluttered but most things are just part of the scenery, which makes it harder to find obscure things like loose bricks. 

This game has a LOT of puzzles where you have to align photos, numbers, etc. and when you click/rotate one thing, 2 others move at once. Drove me nuts.

For the life of me, I could not figure out what the symbols did on the planetarium. I was able to solve all of the puzzles by making educated guesses. 

The epilogue puzzle on the rooftop is infuriating because the programmers used an obscure math system that few people--other than programmers--would know. As a rule of thumb, you should be able to solve puzzle games without requiring outside knowledge.

But despite these nits, it was fun to play and I'd recommend it.

So many things to say about this game. Another amazing puzzle click and point game in the gaming community, with a lot of interactive puzzles and very well hidden objects. It gives a very intricate and misty vibes, since you are surrounded by these "alien like" lights from another planet Ara. 

[b] What does make this game different? [/b]
[list] 
[*]Hidden rooms 
You are able to find multiple hidden rooms through this game by collecting clues that are hidden around the places you are investigating in. Finding special hidden rooms allows you to complete other achievements connected with collectibles, and also find out more lore/story of the game. Not forgetting to mention the rooms are really cool looking, with a special gist given to match the vibes.

[*]Collectibles
Through the entire playthrough, you can find various collectible items, which are connected to multiple achievements. You are completing a collection of figurines, coins, a photo album and paintings. Particular detail i loved about this feature is that you get to see all of your collectibles in the last chapter, all nicely put out on the table. It gives more context to the whole story, and lets you "relive" your game adventure. Also it gives a chance for items to be inspected closely, as they were not inspectable when picked up. 

[*]Being constantly "watched"
Since the game is connected to creatures from another planet, you are constantly being followed by them through the playthrough. It definitely gives an unique experience, and after some time gets quite disturbing, knowing you are constantly being omniously watched. There are no signs story wise that these creatures were harming any of the people residing in the castle, but were tending to become more "friendly" around them the more they were in the castle. They even "accepted" to be studied and torn into pieces for investigating them. Special bond with the creatures is known to be shared with Clementine, as they are very fond of her for the energy she is radiating with. Her connection will be really pointed out at the very end of the game. 

[*]Adorable developer room
When you reach the last chapter, one of the doors you open at the end is like a "shrine" for all people who were working on the game and contributing to it, as well as supporting the people working on the development. I found this really heartwarming and it was presented in a way i never seen before in any other games. There is also a special achievement for this particular room, and it's given for reading the journals of Backer, which contain special messages, even for people who sadly passed away. A very interesting thing was that they also included easter eggs from through the entire playthrough scattered across the room (and very well hidden), so you get to solve the last puzzle and also feel very overwhelmed by all the awesome people who created it. 

[*]Lore - a ton of various ways to write it down
In other games, the only storyline/lore behind the game is usually put on the small piece of paper and it's not even sometimes obligatory to pick up. In this game you have various things to pick up, since you also have an achievement for picking up particular notes and books. You can find journal pages, posters, books - containing paintings, stories and a lot of astrological content (mostly zodiac sign related, as well as the planets). Not to forget there are also computer logs, and clues that help you keep moving, aka. thinking what to do next. 

[*]Special season events
One of the rare puzzle games i've seen that has an Christmas and Halloween event combined in it, with complimentary achievements for both. Sadly i was late for Halloween, so i will need to wait for next year, but i am looking forward to the Christmas one.
[/list]

[b] Why did i like this game particularly? [/b]
I loved the game simply because of it's originality, and a new approach to some things. It's definitely different from other puzzle games i have already played, especially with some of the features i've written beforehand. Though i do have to add, some of the hints are in very tricky locations, and since there can be quite a few rooms, you really need to keep searching and have your brain working at all times, remembering where you found something. Some riddles took me more than an hour just to figure out what to do next.

[b] What would i change? [/b]
If i was able to give advice on what would i change about this game, i'd say adding hints. No need for massive hints to reveal the entire solution, but just to guide you in which direction to go. Since there is many rooms and things to pick up, it's easy to get lost in all the things you need to do. Some parts of the game are also confusing in a way that you oftenly miss clues or missing parts under your nose because they are very well hidden, and you have no clue how to proceed after you did something. Other than that, everything else is brilliant. 

If you get lost or just simply can't find some of the things, and are striving for all the achievements, there are quite a few helpful guides on Steam, which greatly help with revealing the pesky locations of the coins, figurines and photos.

Definitely recommend for all puzzle enjoyers!

Eyes of Ara is an escape room puzzle like game that, in theory and on paper, is a very interesting story- at least as far as I've gotten. 

The problem with the game is that it is too clever for it's players to the point that even the "Spoiler Free Walkthroughs" are too clever to understand. For example- You have to find three orbs for a puzzle, and i found the one I was missing by randomly clicking around in the room the walkthrough said it was in. It was at this point in time that I trashed my attempts to use the steam walkthrough and went to another "spoiler free" one, this time to find the answer for the missing gargoyle head. It too told me where all of them were but it was so painfully "Spoiler free" that I couldn't find it.

It was only going to an actual "Spoilers are here" guide that I discovered that the missing gargoyle head was actually not anywhere that I had access to yet and I needed to do about three more puzzles to find out where it was. 

The game is good, but it's so painfully meant for those "Big Brain Players" (not that I'd ever count myself among them, that most of us normal players are stuck looking for hours on dumb pointless guides that we might as well watch an entire spoiler walk through just to see the end before we even play it ourselves.
